titulo: LOOP-R: the five letters and the nine agents
lead: An agent that evaluates its own work tends to approve itself. LOOP-R, the open INEMA framework that gives this track its name, solves this by separating roles: nine agents, each with what it reads, what it writes, what it decides and what it never does. The five letters give the order of the method. Here you see the design; promoting and rolling back versions belongs to course 5.
objetivo: explain the letters L-O-O-P-R and the contract of the nine agents (reads, writes, decides, never does) and say why the one who does doesn't evaluate.

aprende.t: The nine agents and the contract of each
Why the separation keeps the loop from convincing itself
A real cycle from the example, read in the ledger

hero_alt: Nine small industrial robot figures with dark visors in a circle on a dark technical table.

secoes.titulo: The five letters, in cycle order
secoes.sub: Click each letter: what it asks for and which agents come into it.

itens.t: From X to Y without worsening Z

nos.detalhe: Pick a process that repeats a lot and write the goal with a number: take X to Y without worsening Z. The loop sheet has five answers that no system can safely infer: a goal with a number, where the evidence comes from, what never changes on its own, a cap on cost and time, and who approves. It is the goal from lesson 1, with a guardrail.

nos.sub: always run it the same way
nos.detalhe: The process gets a current version, a short script followed in every run, so that two runs can be compared. The Executor produces the artifact and logs one line. It doesn't opine, doesn't suggest, doesn't change its own prompt.

One line per run, always the same columns, result as yes or no. The Observer turns the lines into evidence: counts by version and variant, no adjectives. If the data doesn't match the schema, it stops the cycle.

The Critic says what worked and what failed, with the strength of the evidence, without proposing a fix. The Optimizer writes hypotheses in the format SE, ENTÃO, PORQUE and MUDANÇA, without repeating discarded ones. The Guardian vetoes anything that touches what never changes or the cap; the veto is final and it doesn't negotiate.

The Experimenter designs the A versus B test, with the minimum sample calculated beforehand. The Evaluator answers one of three: B_GANHOU, A_SEGUE or AMOSTRA_INSUFICIENTE. There is no "it's winning". The Memory records everything without erasing, and the Meta-agent looks at the system (cost, vetoes) and only reports.

secoes.volta: Promoted or discarded, the decision goes to memory and the next cycle starts from the new evidence.
secoes.legenda: Letters as presented in track 2 of the LOOP-R video; agent contracts in loop-r/docs/04-agentes.md and .claude/agents/.

rolagem_fim.titulo: Whoever builds is not whoever inspects
rolagem_fim.texto: Nine separate roles, each reading only what its contract says. It's the separation, not a cleverer prompt, that keeps the loop from convincing itself it improved.
rolagem_fim.curto: Separating roles is the verification in LOOP-R.

secoes.titulo: The contract of the nine, in a table
secoes.sub: Summary of loop-r/docs/02-arquitetura.md, §4. Each agent is a markdown file in .claude/agents/.

blocos.conteudo:
| Agente         | Lê                                  | Escreve                    | Decide                  | Nunca faz                       |
|----------------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Executor       | versoes/atual, entrada da tarefa    | artefato + linha no CSV    | nada                    | mudar o próprio prompt          |
| Observador     | CSV, esquema                        | evidencia.md               | nada                    | interpretar causa               |
| Crítico        | evidência, versão atual, memória    | critica.md                 | se há padrão com N      | propor solução                  |
| Otimizador     | crítica, memória (descartados!)     | hipoteses.md               | nada                    | repetir hipótese descartada     |
| Guardião       | hipóteses, yaml (guarda-corpos, teto)| veto/aprovação por hipótese| veto é final            | ser convencido                  |
| Experimentador | hipóteses aprovadas, amostra mínima | experimento.md             | desenho do teste        | rodar sem N calculado           |
| Avaliador      | resultados A/B, rubrica, calibração | veredito.md                | uma das 3 respostas     | "parece melhor"                 |
| Memória        | tudo do ciclo                       | ledger + 3 arquivos        | nada                    | apagar registro                 |
| Meta-agente    | manifestos de todos os ciclos       | relatorio-meta.md          | nada (v0.1/v1)          | alterar agentes                 |

Four cycles, eight decision lines: two hypotheses vetoed by the Guardian before any test, one discarded by the Evaluator, one promoted to v2.

abas.rot: What is real and what is simulated
abas.html: In the vendas-whatsapp example, the agents really ran; the data is synthetic (1,500 generated rows) and the human decisions are simulated. The example's README separates what is real from what is simulated. Use it to read the mechanism, not as proof of gain.

secoes.sub: Cycle 0002 of the example: the metric went up and the new version still didn't make it in.

texto: Proposals of at most 80 words. It passed the Guardian and went to testing, A against B, 300 runs on each side.
Response rate 19.3% in A against 29.7% in B: significant difference on the target.
But complaints: 6 in 300 against 1 in 300, with zero tolerance on the loop sheet.
A_SEGUE: B only wins if the target goes up and no guardrail drops beyond the tolerance. Both together.
Without this rule, the loop learns to cheat the number.
The hypothesis went to discarded, with the numbers, so it won't be tested again. And the tolerance for rare events was corrected for the next tests, because zero doesn't separate effect from chance.
Promoting and rolling back a version is the subject of course 5.

exercicios.texto: Clone loop-r and open three agents: executor.md, guardiao.md and avaliador.md. For each one, note in agentes.md the "nunca" line from the file.
exercicios.pronto: ls ~/projetos/loop-r/.claude/agents/*.md | wc -l → 9, and grep -ci nunca agentes.md → 3 or more.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · Reading a cycle through the ledger
exercicios.texto: In the vendas-whatsapp example, read the ledger and the verdict of cycle 0002. Write in one sentence why the hypothesis was discarded even though the response rate went up.
exercicios.pronto: grep -c '^| 2026' memoria/ledger.md → 8, and your sentence cites the guardrail (complaints) and the tolerance.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · Separating who does from who evaluates
exercicios.texto: Think of a loop of your own (code, content, support). In agentes.md, write two lines, one starting with executa: and the other with avalia:, and say what the evaluator reads that the executor doesn't write.
exercicios.pronto: grep -cE '^(executa|avalia):' agentes.md → 2, and the "avalia:" line points to a source the executor doesn't control (test, spreadsheet, rubric).

perguntas.p: Why does LOOP-R use nine agents instead of one agent that does and checks?
opcoes: Because nine agents in parallel finish the cycle faster
Because Claude Code requires one agent per role
Because separating them keeps an agent from convincing itself it improved
Because each model can only handle one task at a time without getting lost
perguntas.explica: Doc 04 says: each one reads only what the contract lists and refuses what is under "nunca". An agent that evaluates its own work tends to approve it; separating roles is the verification built into the design.

perguntas.p: B raised the target metric by a significant margin, but worsened a guardrail beyond the tolerance. What is the Evaluator's verdict?
perguntas.explica: B only wins with the target going up AND no guardrail dropping beyond the tolerance. That was the case in cycle 0002 of the example.

perguntas.p: Which agent has a decision that nobody reviews within the cycle?
perguntas.explica: The Guardian's veto is final, it doesn't negotiate and vetoes when in doubt. The Meta-agent, by contrast, decides nothing in the current versions: it only reports.

perguntas.p: What does the vendas-whatsapp example prove?
opcoes: That LOOP-R increases the sales of a real WhatsApp store
That the mechanism runs with real agents, on synthetic data
Nothing: it's just documentation, the agents didn't actually run
That 300 runs are enough for any loop to reach a reliable verdict
perguntas.explica: The agents really ran; the data was generated and the approvals were simulated. Use it to read the mechanism, not as proof of real gain.

itens.texto: Locate the process and the number, Operate the same way every time, Observe in lines, Propose with critique and veto, Reinforce only with a test.
Each agent reads, writes, and decides only what its contract says, and has a list of what it never does.
LOOP-R does not guarantee the number goes up; it guarantees that a worse version does not replace the current one by the system's decision.
